Generated maps, by category

156 generated maps. A category starts with the official maps it is patterned on (marked official); among the re-issues each official original is followed by the maps made from it. Orange tags are playability flags from the mirror-match check.

fortress/ (15 maps)

An open home field at each end behind a kelp wall, fountains only in 1-wide pockets, and a middle that is bare (Stronghold), a maze with small rooms of beds (Trauma), a dense 1-wide maze (Maze) or mazes round an open court (weakhold).

corridors/ (7 maps)

One long dragon per team lies in a column down the middle of the map. The column is 1-wide at its ends, with two fountains in front of the head and two behind the tail, so the dragon starts with two or three free tiles; sealed 3x3 rooms are entered only by a portal whose gate is in the other half of the map.

cells/ (9 maps)

A staggered grid of 2x2 cells of rich beds. A cell opens only through a portal edge inside it, the gate to it stands beside the same cell in the other half, some cells are split so half their beds are decoys, and the two halves of the map never touch.

stripes/ (6 maps)

Bands three rows deep that run right round the map (the sides wrap), joined by one gap near each end of every wall, with trick cells along them: portal edges side by side, a closet entered from the band below, a booth that swaps sides, sealed decoy beds.

lanes/ (7 maps)

1-wide lanes with a fountain at each end (they wrap top to bottom) between 2-wide strips of thin beds; the only ways across are a narrow band through the middle and two short gaps beside the centre strip.

arena/ (10 maps)

The classic maps, where every tile is a bed. A walled arena of richer beds inside a ring three tiles wide, with portals that carry a dragon straight across it; homes that are quarters of the map with a single exit; or Default's nine sealed cells joined into one chain by portals.

tower/ (5 maps)

Each team starts inside a keep wrapped in rings of 1-wide corridor (the official keep, as a stamp); the food worth having is a block of cells in the middle, a long way out.

picture/ (9 maps)

A wrap map of thin beds round one big figure drawn in kelp. Mirrored maps follow Trophy (queens in side chambers, richer beds inside the rim, a portal down the centre line); rotated maps follow Queen Of Spades (a playing card: a frame of kelp inside a ring of thin beds, sealed figures and corner boxes full of beds nobody can reach, and a crown of rich beds whose only way in is a portal from the other team's corner).

islands/ (8 maps)

No rooms and no corridors: hundreds of short strokes of kelp (two in five a single edge, a few long hooked walls) with beds in the nooks and a few portals. The school maps follow Schooltime: the queen coiled in a sealed 2x2 box, the official map's own fish (outlines full of beds with a one-edge mouth and a sealed eye), sealed 2x2 boxes, long outlines, a bed of thin beds along the bottom.

continent/ (6 maps)

The two 64x64 maps added for the Sprint are one drawing made twice: a copy per team, the second turned round, meeting along the middle of a wrap map. Continent maps follow Australia (five states behind straight borders, the starters in the western one and one posted beside the enemy's home, single beds on a lattice, a sealed island behind a portal); campus maps follow Around UNSW (a walled ring round the home, a length-10 dragon lying between two fountain pockets, portals set into the coast).

variants/ (re-issued official maps) (40 maps)

Official maps edited the way the organisers edit them between releases, and official maps with team B mirrored the other way.

behaviour suite (34 maps)

Each map is built round one thing the bot has to get right.
